questions.stem: Shape A has a vertex at (2, 3) and shape B has the corresponding vertex at (−3, 2). The shapes are congruent. Which single transformation maps A to B?

options.text: Reflection in the line y = x

questions.explanation: 90° anticlockwise about origin maps (x, y) to (−y, x). So (2, 3) maps to (−3, 2). This matches. Translation would give (2−5, 3−1) = (−3, 2) also, but we need to check all vertices to determine which. Since the shapes are congruent and the mapping (x,y) to (−y,x) fits, this is a 90° anticlockwise rotation.

questions.stem: Triangle P has vertices (1, 1), (1, 3), (3, 1). Triangle Q has vertices (2, 2), (2, 6), (6, 2). What fully describes the single transformation from P to Q?
questions.explanation: Each coordinate has been multiplied by 2: (1,1)→(2,2), (1,3)→(2,6), (3,1)→(6,2). This is enlargement scale factor 2 centre (0,0). Option (d) doesn't work since (1,1)+(1,1)=(2,2) but (3,1)+(1,1)=(4,2) not (6,2).

questions.stem: A shape is mapped to its image so that every point (x, y) becomes (x, −y). Which transformation is this?
questions.explanation: The mapping (x, y) → (x, −y) keeps the x-coordinate the same and negates the y-coordinate. This is a reflection in the x-axis. Reflection in the y-axis would give (−x, y).

questions.stem: Shape A is mapped to shape B by a single transformation. A has side lengths 5 cm and B has corresponding side lengths 15 cm. B is on the opposite side of a fixed point from A. What type of transformation is this?
questions.explanation: The sides are 3 times larger, so |scale factor| = 3. Since the image is on the opposite side of the centre, the scale factor is negative: −3. When describing an enlargement fully, you must state 'enlargement', the scale factor, and the centre.

questions.stem: Which of the following transformations does NOT preserve the orientation (sense) of a shape?
questions.explanation: Reflection reverses the orientation of a shape (a clockwise labelling becomes anticlockwise). Translations, rotations, and positive enlargements all preserve orientation. This is why reflected shapes appear 'flipped'.
